newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDES HEAD ALL-STAR LIST.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-SWEDES HEAD ALL-STAR LIST.

text.p: Sweden dominated the all-star selections at the ice hockey world championship on Tuesday.
Sweden's Michael Nylander, rumoured to be headed to the NHL's Calgary Flames next season, was named all-star centre between high-scoring Czech wingers Vladimir Vujtek and Martin Prochazka.
The two Czechs, who caught the interest of the Toronto Maple Leafs with their strong play in the tournament, tied for the scoring lead with seven goals and 14 points.
Los Angeles Kings defenceman Rob Blake was the only Canadian to make the squad. He was joined on the blueline by the Phoenix Coyotes' Teppo Numminen of Finland.
The New York Islanders' Tommy Salo of Sweden was named all-star netminder, having posted a sparkling 1.88 goals against average.
The all-star coach is Sweden's Kent Forsberg, who will lead the country's entry at the Nagano Olympics next season.
Sweden were playing the second game of the best-of-three final for the title on Tuesday, having won Sunday's first game 3-2.
